normal.cn: shiver 更偏冷，shudder 更偏恶心，tremble 居中。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of water held by two hands that will not keep still.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手端着一杯水，怎么也拿不稳。

abstract.en: Watch the circles spread from the rim inward.
abstract.cn: 看着水纹从杯壁往里散。

abstract.en: Then let a leaf do the same thing on a bare branch.
abstract.cn: 再让一片叶子在光枝上做同样的动作。

examples.en: Her voice trembled as she read the letter aloud.
examples.cn: 她大声读信时声音在发颤。

examples.en: The old bridge trembled under the weight of the lorry.
examples.cn: 老桥在卡车的重量下颤动。

examples.en: He trembled at the thought of speaking in public.
examples.cn: 一想到公开发言他就心慌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吞不乐」——冻得吞下不开心，浑身抖个不停。

root: 拉丁语 tremere（抖动），经古法语 trembler 进入英语；同族有 tremor、tremulous

sensesIntro.en: One small, fast shaking, whether it runs through a body, a leaf, or the ground.
sensesIntro.cn: 就是一种又小又快的抖动，无论在身体里、叶子上还是地面上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands holding a cup that will not stay still.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手端着怎么也端不稳的杯子。

branches.en: The body senses, first from cold and fear, then from anger and joy.
branches.cn: 身体义：先因寒冷与恐惧，再因愤怒与激动。

branches.en: The object sense, where leaves and bridges shake too.
branches.cn: 物体义：叶子与桥也会抖。

branches.en: The inner sense, where only the feeling shakes.
branches.cn: 内心义：抖的只是那份心情。

branches.en: The noun sense, a name for the shaking itself.
branches.cn: 名词义：给这种抖动本身起名。

branches.en: The default image: cold hands at a bus stop.
branches.cn: 默认画面：车站上冻僵的手。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of shaking with a frequentative air, worn down by French.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「抖动」动词，带反复意味，经法语磨圆了形状。

latinIntro.en: Trem- stays visible in tremor and tremulous, both closer to the Latin.
latinIntro.cn: trem- 在 tremor 与 tremulous 里仍然看得见，两者都更接近拉丁原形。

items.example: The stem gives tremor and tremulous.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干生出 tremor 与 tremulous。

items.meaningCN: 经法语来自拉丁 -ulare 的动词词尾

items.exampleCN: 一阵震动震得窗户直响。

items.example: The dog trembled in the rain.
The bridge trembled for a moment.

items.meaningCN: 构成现在分词与动名词

definition_zh: 巨大的；极大的；极好的；了不起的
definition_en: extremely great in size, amount, or effect, or extremely good
core_image: 一面山壁横在眼前，仰头看到脖颈发酸才见顶
scene: 站在峡谷边抬头，两壁高得让人后退半步，风从下面直往上冲。The canyon drops a tremendous distance to the river.
sceneCN: 这里 tremendous 是「巨大的」（第 1 个义项：体积、数量或影响极大）；句意为峡谷到河面的落差极大。仰头看不清顶的山壁正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：极好的；了不起的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「极大地；非常」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「巨大」
同根名词，义为「震动；颤栗」

senses.title: Extremely great in size
senses.definition: very great in size, extent, or degree
senses.definitionCN: 在体积、范围或程度上非常大
senses.example: They crossed a tremendous desert.
senses.exampleCN: 他们穿过一片巨大的沙漠。
senses.why: A thing so great that one trembles at it is simply great in size, which is the direct descendant.
senses.whyCN: 大到让人发抖之物，直接就成了「体积巨大」，这是最直接的后代义。

senses.title: Extremely great in amount
senses.definition: very large in number or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 在数量上很大
senses.example: A tremendous number of people came.
senses.exampleCN: 来了极多的人。
senses.why: Number is only size counted, so the same adjective moves from space to quantity.
senses.whyCN: 数量不过是数出来的体积，所以同一个形容词从空间挪到数目上。

senses.title: Extremely strong in force
senses.definition: very strong in effect or force
senses.definitionCN: 在效力或影响上非常强
senses.example: The plan met tremendous opposition.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划遭到极大的反对。
senses.why: Force that makes people tremble is the sense closest to the Latin, applied to effect rather than body.
senses.whyCN: 让人发抖的力量最接近拉丁原义，只是作用在效果而非身体上。

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: excellent or wonderful, in everyday approval
senses.definitionCN: 在日常赞许中表示「很棒」
senses.example: We had a tremendous time.
senses.exampleCN: 我们玩得非常开心。
senses.why: Weakened further, the awe becomes everyday praise for something excellent.
senses.whyCN: 再弱化一步，那份敬畏就变成对好东西的日常夸赞。

senses.title: Arousing awe or dread
senses.definition: so great as to cause wonder or fear, the oldest sense
senses.definitionCN: 大到令人惊叹或畏惧，这是最古老的义项
senses.example: The storm came on with tremendous force,
senses.exampleCN: 风暴以令人畏惧的力量袭来。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: tremendus names what must be trembled at.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：tremendus 指的就是「必须对它发抖」之物。

intro.en: The word is Latin tremendus, to be trembled at, from tremere, to tremble.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语 tremendus，意为「令人发抖的」，出自动词 tremere（发抖）。

items.en: Tremere means to tremble, and tremendus is the thing one must tremble at.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tremere 意为发抖，tremendus 就是「必须对它发抖」之物。

items.en: The Latin gerundive ending -ndus marks something that ought to be feared or done.
items.cn: 拉丁动形词词尾 -ndus 标记「应该被畏惧或应做」之物。

items.en: English first uses the word for things that inspire awe and dread.
items.cn: 英语最初用这个词指引起敬畏与恐惧的事物。

items.en: In the nineteenth century it weakens into a general word for very great.
items.cn: 十九世纪它弱化为泛指「非常大」的词。

items.en: Recent usage adds an everyday sense of very good.
items.cn: 近期用法又添上「非常好」的日常义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the trem- root of trembling, while the near-meaning group gathers other words for very large.
note.cn: 形近组共用 trem-（发抖）词根，近义组汇集表示极大的其他词。

entries.definition: to shake slightly
a slight shaking
shaking, or timid
to a very great degree
very large indeed
extremely large
extremely wide in area
as large as a giant statue

normalIntro.en: The word contains tremble, and it once meant something that made you tremble.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词里含着 tremble，它原先指让人发抖的东西。

normal.en: Tremere is to tremble, so tremendous means to be trembled at.
normal.cn: tremere 是发抖，所以 tremendous 就是「令人发抖的」。

normal.en: Over time the trembling became mere size, and the word now means very great.
normal.cn: 久而久之，那份颤抖只剩下「大」，如今意为极大。

normal.en: Tremor and tremulous share the same root, so they are one family.
normal.cn: tremor 与 tremulous 同根，属于一个家族。

normal.en: The adverb tremendously means to a great degree.
normal.cn: 副词 tremendously 意为「极大地」。

normal.en: In speech it also means very good, as in a tremendous day.
normal.cn: 口语里也表示很好，如 a tremendous day。

abstract.en: Picture a cliff so high that your neck aches to see the top.
abstract.cn: 想象一面山壁高到抬头看到脖子酸。

abstract.en: Feel the small tremble in your legs at the edge.
abstract.cn: 感受站在边沿时腿上的那阵轻颤。

abstract.en: Then let the same shake become praise for a good meal.
abstract.cn: 再让这阵颤动变成对一顿好饭的称赞。

examples.en: The project required a tremendous amount of work.
examples.cn: 这个项目需要大量的工作。

examples.en: She felt tremendous pressure before the exam.
examples.cn: 考试前她感到巨大的压力。

examples.en: You did a tremendous job on the report.
examples.cn: 这份报告你做得非常出色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿门得死」——门大得要穿过去都累死，真是巨大。

root: 拉丁语 tremere（发抖）的动形词 tremendus（令人发抖的）；同族有 tremble、tremor、tremulous

sensesIntro.en: All senses descend from awe: something so great that a person trembles at it.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都源自敬畏：某物大到让人发抖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cliff so high the neck aches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面高到脖子发酸的山壁。

branches.en: The size and number senses, the plain modern use.
branches.cn: 体积与数量义：现代最普通的用法。

branches.en: The force sense, where the effect is overwhelming.
branches.cn: 力量义：影响压倒一切。

branches.en: The praise sense, borrowed from admiring talk.
branches.cn: 赞扬义：从赞赏的话里借来。

branches.en: The awe sense, the oldest and most literal.
branches.cn: 敬畏义：最古老也最字面。

branches.en: The cliff sense, the plain picture of size.
branches.cn: 峭壁义：体积最朴素的画面。

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin gerundive, a form that marks what ought to be feared or done.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是拉丁动形词，这种形式标记「应被畏惧或应做的事」。

latinIntro.en: The trem- stem gives tremble, tremor, tremulous, and tremendous.
latinIntro.cn: trem- 词干生出 tremble、tremor、tremulous 与 tremendous。

items.example: The stem gives tremor and tremble.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干生出 tremor 与 tremble。

items.example: Tremendus is the source of tremendous.
items.exampleCN: tremendus 是 tremendous 的来源。

items.example: Even the suffix -ous survives in tremendous.
items.exampleCN: 连 -ous 这个形容词词尾都留在 tremendous 里。

items.example: A tremor ran through the floor.

items.meaning: to be trembled at, hence huge
items.example: A tremendous wave hit the wall.
The tremendousness of the task scared them.
items.exampleCN: 任务的巨大让他们害怕。

definition_zh: 三角形；三角板；三角关系；三角铁
definition_en: a flat shape with three straight sides and three angles, or an object of that shape
core_image: 三根直棍首尾相接，围出一块有三个角的空地
scene: 黑板上，老师用三条直直的粉笔线围出一块封闭的图形，量角器摆在旁边。Draw a triangle with two equal sides.
sceneCN: 这里 triangle 是「三角形」（第 1 个义项：三条边三个角的平面图形）；句意为画一个两边相等的三角形。三根线首尾相连围出一块地的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 名词换词尾 -ular 构成形容词，义为「三角形的」
由形容词加 -ate 构成动词，义为「用三角测量；使成三角形」
由动词加 -ion 构成名词，义为「三角测量法」

senses.title: A shape with three sides
senses.definition: a flat figure bounded by three straight sides and having three angles
senses.definitionCN: 由三条直边围成、有三个角的平面图形
senses.example: The flag has a red triangle in the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 旗子一角有个红色三角形。
senses.why: The word simply says three angles: tri- is three and gonia is angle in Greek.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面就是「三个角」：tri- 是希腊语的三，gonia 是角。

senses.title: A set square or musical instrument
senses.definition: a flat three-sided tool for drawing or measuring, or a steel rod bent into that shape and struck
senses.definitionCN: 画图测量用的三边形板，或弯成三边形、用来敲击的钢条
senses.example: He played the triangle in the school orchestra.
senses.exampleCN: 他在学校乐队里敲三角铁。
senses.why: An object made in three-sided form takes the name of the form itself.
senses.whyCN: 做成三边形的物件，直接承接了这个形状的名字。

senses.title: A group of three people
senses.definition: a situation in which three people are closely and often awkwardly involved
senses.definitionCN: 三个人紧密牵扯、常常尴尬的局面
senses.example: The novel is built on a love triangle.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说建立在一个三角恋上。
senses.why: Three people pull on one another the way three sides close a figure, so the word pictures the group.
senses.whyCN: 三个人彼此拉扯，正像三条边围住一个图形，于是这个词用来画这种关系。

senses.title: A three-sided area of land or route
senses.definition: a three-sided piece of land, or a route that returns to its start
senses.definitionCN: 呈三角形的地块，或绕回起点的航路
senses.example: The plane flew the triangle between three islands.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机在三座岛之间飞了个三角圈。
senses.why: Any three points can be joined into a closed figure, so a journey among three places borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 任意三点都能连成一个闭合图形，所以三点之间的行程也借用了这个名字。

intro.en: The word is Latin triangulum, a three-cornered figure, from tri-, three, and angulus, a corner.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语 triangulum，即「三角之物」，由 tri-（三）与 angulus（角）构成。

items.en: The root treyes supplies three, and the same root appears in trio and triple.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 treyes 提供「三」，也出现在 trio 与 triple 里。

items.en: Angulus means a corner or an angle, and gives angle, anchor, and anxious through its relatives.
items.cn: 拉丁语 angulus 意为角落、角，其亲族生出 angle、anchor 与 anxious。

items.en: Triangulum means having three corners and is used both of shapes and of land.
items.cn: 拉丁语 triangulum 意为「有三个角」，既指图形也指地块。

items.en: Old French triangle passes the word into English with the plain shape sense.
items.cn: 古法语 triangle 把这个词传入英语，含义就是那个图形。

items.en: Music and later surveying give the word its instrument and its measuring senses.
items.cn: 音乐与后来的测量学给了它乐器和测量用语的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tri- and -angul- pieces, while the near-meaning group gathers other plane figures.
note.cn: 形近组共用 tri- 与 -angul- 两部分，近义组汇集其他平面图形。

entries.definition: having three sides
the space between two meeting lines
three times as much
a three-pronged spear; the prefix is shared, the root differs
entries.definitionCN: 三叉戟；只是前缀相同，词根不同

entries.definition: a figure with four right angles
a figure with four equal sides
any figure with many straight sides
a piece shaped like a narrow triangle

normalIntro.en: Tri- is three and angle is angle, so the word explains itself.
normalIntro.cn: tri- 是三，angle 是角，这个词自己就把意思说清了。

normal.en: Tri- appears in tripod, triple, and trio, all about three.
normal.cn: tri- 出现在 tripod、triple、trio 里，全都与三有关。

normal.en: Angle is the same word as the one in right angle.
normal.cn: angle 就是 right angle 里的那个 angle。

normal.en: Triangular is the adjective, with -ular replacing the -e.
normal.cn: triangular 是形容词，-ular 替掉了词尾的 -e。

normal.en: A love triangle has three sides that pull against each other.
normal.cn: 三角恋的三条边彼此拉扯。

normal.en: A triangle in an orchestra is a steel rod struck with a stick.
normal.cn: 乐队里的三角铁是一根被小棒敲的钢条。

abstract.en: Picture three matchsticks laid end to end, closing a small yard.
abstract.cn: 想象三根火柴首尾相接，围出一小块院子。

abstract.en: See the angles as three corners the sticks cannot round off.
abstract.cn: 把三个角想成火柴磨不圆的三处尖角。

abstract.en: Set the same yard on three islands and fly around it.
abstract.cn: 把这块院子搁在三座岛上，再绕它飞一圈。

examples.en: The roof is built from two large triangles.
examples.cn: 屋顶由两个大三角形构成。

examples.en: She tapped the triangle once and the hall fell silent.
examples.cn: 她敲了一下三角铁，礼堂立刻安静下来。

examples.en: Their friendship became a triangle when a third classmate joined.
examples.cn: 第三个同学加入后，他们的友谊成了三角。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「揣安钩」——揣着三个安好的钩子，钩成三角形的三个角。

root: 拉丁语 tri-（三）+ angulus（角），名词 triangulum 经古法语进入英语；同族有 angle、triangular、triple

sensesIntro.en: The word names a shape first, then any object or group that takes that shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先给形状命名，再给任何取这一形状的物件或群体命名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three straight sticks closing a small plot of ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：三根直棍围出一小块地。

branches.en: The plain geometric sense, the shape itself.
branches.cn: 朴素几何义：形状本身。

branches.en: The instrument sense, where a made object takes the shape’s name.
branches.cn: 器物义：做成这个形状的东西直接用了名字。

branches.en: The human sense, where three people pull against one another.
branches.cn: 人事义：三个人彼此拉扯。

branches.en: The spatial sense, where land or a route forms the figure.
branches.cn: 空间义：地块或航路形成这个图形。

branches.en: The geometric sense again, where the three corners are what matters.
branches.cn: 再回几何义：关键在三个角。

intro.en: The word joins a Greek-derived number to a Latin word for corner.
intro.cn: 这个词把表示数字的前缀与拉丁语「角」一词连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Angulus is behind angle, triangular, and the whole family of English angle words.
latinIntro.cn: angulus 支撑着 angle、triangular 以及整族英语「角」类词。

items.example: The angle is nearly ninety degrees.

items.exampleCN: 这支三重奏演奏了一整晚。

definition_zh: 诡计；把戏；窍门；戏弄；哄骗
definition_en: a clever act meant to deceive or amuse someone, or to deceive a person in that way
core_image: 一只手把硬币从这个人眼前晃过，却从那人耳后取出
scene: 街头围了一圈人，那个戴帽子的男人把手绢一晃，鸽子从袖口飞了出来。He knows a trick that makes a coin disappear.
sceneCN: 这里 trick 是「戏法、把戏」（第 2 个义项：逗人一乐的巧妙手法）；句意为他会一个让硬币消失的戏法。手一晃、东西换个地方出现，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 名词加 -y 构成形容词，义为「棘手的；狡猾的」
名词加 -ery 构成，义为「欺骗行径」
名词加 -ster 构成，义为「骗子；恶作剧者」

senses.title: A plan to deceive someone
senses.definition: a clever but dishonest plan to get something from someone
senses.definitionCN: 巧妙却不老实、想从别人那里得利的计谋
senses.example: It was a trick to make him sign the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个骗他签字的诡计。
senses.why: The word comes from Old French trickier, to deceive, and its oldest sense is a cheat or a deceit.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自古法语 trickier（欺骗），最早的义项就是骗人或骗术。

senses.title: A clever act that amuses
senses.definition: a skilful performance, such as a card trick, done to entertain
senses.definitionCN: 为逗乐而做的熟练表演，如纸牌戏法
senses.example: The children loved the card trick.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们很喜欢那个纸牌戏法。
senses.why: A cheat and a magic show differ only in intent: both turn on a hidden method.
senses.whyCN: 骗人的手法与魔术表演只差用心：两者都靠一套藏着的方法。

senses.title: A clever way of doing something
senses.definition: a special way of doing a task that makes it easier
senses.definitionCN: 让事情变容易的特殊做法
senses.example: The trick is to stir the sauce slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 窍门是慢慢地搅酱汁。
senses.why: The hidden method that deceived someone can also simply help: then we call it the trick.
senses.whyCN: 那套藏着的方法如果不为骗人而是帮忙，我们就叫它窍门。

senses.title: To deceive someone
senses.definition: to make someone believe something untrue so that you gain an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 让人相信不实之事以取得好处
senses.example: They tricked him out of his savings.
senses.exampleCN: 他们骗走了他的存款。
senses.why: The verb is the act behind the noun: to work the hidden method on a person.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词背后的动作：把藏着的方法用在某个人身上。

senses.title: A habit or mannerism
senses.definition: a peculiar habit of speech or behaviour that a person is known for
senses.definitionCN: 某人为人熟知的言语或举止习惯
senses.example: He has a trick of raising one eyebrow.
senses.exampleCN: 他有个挑一挑眉的习惯。
senses.why: A repeated piece of behaviour becomes as automatic as a practised sleight.
senses.whyCN: 反复出现的小动作，会像练熟的手法一样成为本能。

intro.en: The word comes from Old French trique, a deceit or a cheat, and the verb trickier, to deceive.
intro.cn: 这个词来自古法语 trique（欺骗、诈术）与动词 trickier（欺骗）。

items.en: Trique means a deceit, a shift, or a cheating play, and is used of dice and dealings.
items.cn: 古法语 trique 意为诈术、花招、骗人的把戏，用于骰子与交易。

items.en: English borrows the noun in the fifteenth century for a deceitful act.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个名词，指欺诈行为。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word covers harmless sleight of hand and card play.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词已涵盖无害的手法与纸牌戏法。

items.en: Later it names the clever knack of a trade and the odd habit of a person.
items.cn: 后来又用来指行业的技巧与一个人的怪癖。

items.en: The ultimate origin is uncertain; the word may be related to Old French trichier, to cheat.
items.cn: 最终来源不确定；可能和古法语 trichier（欺骗）有关。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words differing by one letter or sharing the stem, while the near-meaning group names other deceptions and knacks.
note.cn: 形近组汇集只差一个字母或共用词干的短词，近义组列出其他骗术与诀窍。

entries.definition: difficult or requiring care
the use of tricks to deceive
a large road vehicle
to flow in a thin slow stream
a playful trick on someone
to make someone believe what is false
a special skill at doing something
a false appearance made by a performer

normalIntro.en: Five letters, one sharp sound, and a family that grows from it.
normalIntro.cn: 五个字母，一个短促的音，还长出一整个词族。

normal.en: Tricky adds -y and means full of tricks, so difficult.
normal.cn: tricky 加 -y，意为满是机关，所以是棘手。

normal.en: Trickery adds -ery and names the practice of deceiving.
normal.cn: trickery 加 -ery，指欺骗的行径。

normal.en: A trickster is the person who plays the tricks.
normal.cn: trickster 就是耍弄这些把戏的人。

normal.en: Do the trick means the method works, with no deceit at all.
normal.cn: do the trick 指办法奏效，毫无欺骗之意。

normal.en: The verb takes a direct object and usually into: trick him into signing.
normal.cn: 这个动词带宾语，常加 into：trick him into signing。

abstract.en: Picture a coin leaving one palm and appearing behind an ear.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币离开一只手心，却出现在耳后。

abstract.en: Watch the empty palm open flat to prove nothing is there.
abstract.cn: 看那只空手摊平，证明什么也没有。

abstract.en: Then put that same sleight into a recipe and call it the trick.
abstract.cn: 再把这套手法放进菜谱里，就叫做窍门。

examples.en: The old trick of hiding a key under a flowerpot failed.
examples.cn: 把钥匙藏在花盆下这个老花招不管用了。

examples.en: It took me a while to learn the trick of folding the dough.
examples.cn: 我花了好一阵才学会折面团的窍门。

examples.en: They tricked the old man into paying twice.
examples.cn: 他们骗那位老人付了两次钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踹克」——一脚踹开攻克对手的诡计，全靠手法。

root: 古法语 trique（诈术）与动词 trickier（欺骗），十五世纪进入英语；同族有 tricky、trickery、trickster，最终来源不确定

sensesIntro.en: One hidden method runs through every sense: it may cheat, amuse, help, or simply become a habit.
sensesIntro.cn: 一套藏着的方法贯穿所有义项：它可以骗人、逗乐、帮忙，或干脆变成一个习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin that leaves one palm and appears elsewhere.
core.cn: 核心意象：硬币离开一只手心，在别处出现。

branches.en: The deceitful sense, where the method is used against someone.
branches.cn: 欺骗义：那套方法被用来对付人。

branches.en: The performing sense, where the method only entertains.
branches.cn: 表演义：那套方法只为逗乐。

branches.en: The helpful sense, where the same method makes work easy.
branches.cn: 助人义：同一套方法让活变简单。

branches.en: The verb sense, where the method is set in motion.
branches.cn: 动词义：把那套方法使出来。

branches.en: The habitual sense, where a mannerism repeats like a practised move.
branches.cn: 习惯义：小动作像练熟的手法一样重复。

intro.en: The word is short, but it builds a family with three productive suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词很短，却靠三个能产的词尾长出一族词。

latinIntro.en: The French source has no Latin relatives in English, so the Latin list here stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 它的法语来源在英语里没有拉丁亲族，所以这里的拉丁同源词留空。

items.example: He played a trick on us.

items.exampleCN: 一道棘手的题难住了所有人。

items.example: The trickster fooled the whole village.

items.exampleCN: 这条小路刁钻地往山下走。

items.example: He underestimated the trickiness of the task.
items.exampleCN: 他低估了这件事的棘手程度。

items.meaning: a question designed to catch you

items.example: The children shouted trick or treat.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们喊着不给糖就捣蛋。

items.example: The move looked tricky, even trickish.
items.exampleCN: 这一步看着就刁，甚至有点诡。

definition_zh: 修剪；整理；削减；整齐的；修长的
definition_en: to cut a small amount from something to make it neat, or to reduce an amount; neat and well shaped
core_image: 一把剪刀沿着边线走一圈，多出来的毛边落在地上
scene: 花园里，园丁拿长剪沿着绿篱一路剪过去，剪口平得像一条线。He trims the hedge every Saturday morning.
sceneCN: 这里 trim 是「修剪」（第 1 个义项：剪去多余部分使其整齐）；句意为他每周六早上修剪绿篱。剪刀沿线走、毛边落地的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 现在分词名词化，义为「修剪；装饰边；配料」
动词加 -er 构成，义为「修剪者；修剪工具」
形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「整齐；整洁」

senses.title: To cut something neat
senses.definition: to cut a small amount off something so that it looks tidy
senses.definitionCN: 剪掉一点使某物看起来整齐
senses.example: She trimmed the rose bushes back.
senses.exampleCN: 她把玫瑰丛修剪了一遍。
senses.why: The old verb means to make ready or to arrange, and neat cutting is the way such arranging is done.
senses.whyCN: 这个古动词意为「整理、备好」，而剪整齐正是整理的做法。

senses.title: To reduce an amount
senses.definition: to make a sum, a list, or a text smaller by removing parts
senses.definitionCN: 去掉一部分，使金额、清单或文字变小
senses.example: The council trimmed the spending plan.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会削减了开支计划。
senses.why: Cutting a hedge and cutting a budget are the same motion: taking off what sticks out.
senses.whyCN: 剪树篱与削预算都是同一个动作：把多出来的部分去掉。

senses.title: To decorate an edge
senses.definition: to add a border or ornament to the edge of something
senses.definitionCN: 在某物的边上加饰边或装饰
senses.example: The dress is trimmed with lace.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子镶了花边。
senses.why: The word also meant to fit out or equip, and decorating an edge is part of that outfitting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也曾表示装配、置办，而给边镶饰正是装配的一部分。

senses.title: Neat and well shaped
senses.definition: looking neat, slim, and in good order
senses.definitionCN: 看起来整洁、匀称、有精神
senses.example: He keeps a trim little garden.
senses.exampleCN: 他把小花园打理得很整齐。
senses.why: What has been trimmed looks trim: the adjective is the result of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 被修剪过的东西显得整齐：形容词就是动词的结果。

senses.title: To adjust the balance of a boat
senses.definition: to arrange the load or sails of a boat so that it sits level
senses.definitionCN: 调整船的负载或帆，使船身平稳
senses.example: The crew trimmed the sails before the wind rose.
senses.exampleCN: 风起前船员调好了帆。
senses.why: Balancing a boat is tidying a different edge, so the same word serves on water.
senses.whyCN: 给船找平是在整理另一条边，于是同一个词也用在水上。

intro.en: The verb is an old English word for making ready or arranging, and neat cutting is its oldest surviving sense.
intro.cn: 这个动词是古英语里表示准备、整理的老词，剪整齐是它保存下来的最早义项。

items.en: Trymman means to make firm, to strengthen, or to arrange a thing.
items.cn: 古英语 trymman 意为使牢固、增强，或把事物安排好。

items.en: The word narrows towards tidying edges, and is used of hair, cloth, and hedges.
items.cn: 这个词逐渐收窄到整理边缘，用于头发、布料与树篱。

items.en: Commerce gives it the sense of cutting down a sum or a staff.
items.cn: 商业给了它削减金额或人员的义项。

items.en: Nautical use keeps an older sense of setting a load or sail in balance.
items.cn: 航海用法保留了「把负载或帆调平衡」的较老义项。

items.en: The adjective grows from the noun, naming what has just been made neat.
items.cn: 形容词由名词生出，用来指刚被弄整齐的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words close in spelling or root, while the near-meaning group names other cuts and states of neatness.
note.cn: 形近组汇集拼写或词根相近的短词，近义组列出其他剪切与整洁状态。

entries.definition: a journey or a stumble
the outer edge of something
a tool or person that trims
to shake slightly
entries.definitionCN: 发抖；只是开头写法相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to cut back branches
to cut a small piece off
tidy and in good order
thin in an attractive way

normalIntro.en: Think of the barber’s shop and of a budget: the same short word cuts both.
normalIntro.cn: 想想理发店与预算：同一个短词，两边都能剪。

normal.en: The past tense doubles the m: trimmed.
normal.cn: 过去式双写 m：trimmed。

normal.en: Trimmer is the tool or the person, trimming is the cut-off pieces.
normal.cn: trimmer 是工具或人，trimming 是剪下来的碎料。

normal.en: Trim the hedge, trim the budget, and trim the sails all mean tidy an edge.
normal.cn: 剪树篱、削预算、调帆，都是在整理一条边。

normal.en: In trim means in good condition, especially of a body or a boat.
normal.cn: in trim 指状态良好，尤其指身材或船。

normal.en: The adjective and the verb share one spelling.
normal.cn: 形容词与动词拼写完全相同。

abstract.en: Hear the snip of shears running along a straight hedge.
abstract.cn: 听长剪沿着笔直的树篱一路咔嚓。

abstract.en: See the green bits fall and the top become a line.
abstract.cn: 看绿屑落下，顶面变成一条线。

abstract.en: Then hold the same shears over a sheet of numbers.
abstract.cn: 再把同一把剪子悬在一张数字表上。

examples.en: Could you trim a little off the back, please?
examples.cn: 后面能帮我修掉一点吗？

examples.en: The firm trimmed fifty jobs from the plant.
examples.cn: 公司从厂里削减了五十个岗位。

examples.en: The boat looked trim and ready for the race.
examples.cn: 这条船看起来整洁挺括，随时能比赛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹姆」——对着刘海吹一口，再拿剪子修整齐。

root: 古英语 trymman（使牢固、整理），后收窄为「修剪边缘」；同族有 trimming、trimmer、trimness

sensesIntro.en: The senses all start from tidying an edge, then spread to money, ornament, appearance, and balance.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项都从「整理边缘」出发，再扩到钱、饰边、外形与平衡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shears running along a hedge, leaving a straight line.
core.cn: 核心意象：长剪沿着树篱走，留下一条直线。

branches.en: The cutting sense, where an edge is made neat.
branches.cn: 修剪义：把边剪整齐。

branches.en: The reducing sense, where a sum is cut down.
branches.cn: 削减义：把数字剪小。

branches.en: The decorating sense, where an edge is dressed.
branches.cn: 装饰义：给边加打扮。

branches.en: The adjective and the nautical senses, where the result is order and balance.
branches.cn: 形容词与航海义：结果是秩序与平衡。

branches.en: The hedge sense again, where the shears do the tidying.
branches.cn: 再回修剪义：干这份活的是长剪。

intro.en: The word is short and Germanic, and its suffixes are the common English ones.
intro.cn: 这个词短小且属日耳曼语，词尾都是常见的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin relative in English, so the Latin list here stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 它在英语里没有拉丁亲族，所以这里的拉丁同源词留空。

items.example: Trim the edges with a knife.

items.meaning: keeps the short vowel before a suffix
items.meaningCN: 词尾加缀时双写辅音以保短元音
items.example: Trim gives trimmed in the past, not trimed.
items.exampleCN: trim 的过去式是 trimmed，不是 trimed。

items.example: The untrimmed hedge blocked the path.
items.exampleCN: 没修剪的树篱把路挡住了。

definition_zh: 胜利；成功；得意；凯旋；战胜
definition_en: a great victory or success, or the joy felt after winning
core_image: 胜利者站在高处，人群沿街欢呼，花环从车窗上垂下来
scene: 最后一球落地，全场观众站起来，球员把球衣举过头顶。The team’s triumph in the final was greeted with fireworks.
sceneCN: 这里 triumph 是「胜利」（第 1 个义项：一场重大的胜利）；句意为球队在决赛中的胜利在烟火中受到欢庆。球场沸腾的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 名词加 -al 构成形容词，义为「凯旋的；庆祝胜利的」
名词加 -ant 构成形容词，义为「获胜的；得意洋洋的」
形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「得意地；胜利地」

senses.title: A great victory
senses.definition: a very great victory or a notable success after a struggle
senses.definitionCN: 经过斗争取得的重大胜利或显著成功
senses.example: The climb was a triumph over fear.
senses.exampleCN: 这次攀登是对恐惧的一次胜利。
senses.why: The Latin triumphus names the procession of a victorious general into Rome.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 triumphus 指得胜将军列队进入罗马的凯旋式。

senses.title: The joy of winning
senses.definition: the strong feeling of joy and pride that follows a victory
senses.definitionCN: 胜利之后强烈的喜悦与自豪
senses.example: She could not hide her triumph when the results came.
senses.exampleCN: 结果出来时，她掩不住得意。
senses.why: The procession was a public show of joy, and the word keeps that feeling.
senses.whyCN: 凯旋式本就是把喜悦公开出来，这个词把那份情绪也保留下来。

senses.title: To win or overcome
senses.definition: to gain a victory over an opponent, a difficulty, or a weakness
senses.definitionCN: 战胜对手、困难或弱点
senses.example: Good sense triumphed over panic.
senses.exampleCN: 理智战胜了恐慌。
senses.why: The verb turns the procession into an act: to be the one led home in honour.
senses.whyCN: 动词把凯旋式变成一个动作：成为被光荣迎回的那个人。

senses.title: An outstanding achievement
senses.definition: a work or result that stands far above others
senses.definitionCN: 远超同类的作品或成果
senses.example: The bridge is a triumph of engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是工程的杰作。
senses.why: Any great finished work can be met with the applause once given to a returning general.
senses.whyCN: 任何完成的伟大作品，都能得到当年献给凯旋将军的那份掌声。

intro.en: The word comes from Latin triumphus, the honour paid to a victorious general entering Rome.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 triumphus，是给得胜将军进入罗马时所受的荣典。

items.en: Triumphus names the ceremonial entry of a victorious commander into the city of Rome.
items.cn: 拉丁语 triumphus 指得胜统帅列队进入罗马城的仪式。

items.en: The word is probably borrowed into Latin from Greek thriambos, a hymn to Dionysus sung in procession.
items.cn: 这个词大概是从希腊语 thriambos 借入拉丁语的，那是列队所唱的狄俄尼索斯颂歌。

items.en: Old French triumphe passes the word into English with its victory sense.
items.cn: 古法语 triumphe 把这个词连同胜利义传入英语。

items.en: English uses the noun first of the Roman ceremony, then of any great victory.
items.cn: 英语先用这个名词指罗马的仪式，后指任何重大胜利。

items.en: The senses widen to the feeling of victory and to any outstanding achievement.
items.cn: 后来又扩及胜利的感受与任何卓越成就。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin triumph- stem, while the near-meaning group gathers other words for winning.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁语 triumph- 词干，近义组汇集其他表示取胜的词。

entries.definition: celebrating a victory
having won or showing joy at winning
a brass wind instrument
entries.definitionCN: 小号；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a card that beats the others
entries.definitionCN: 王牌；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the act of winning a battle or contest
the achieving of a goal
great honour and praise
the losing of a battle or contest

normalIntro.en: Hear the trumpet in triumph, and see the arch in the street.
normalIntro.cn: 在 triumph 里听出 trumpet 的号声，再看街道上的凯旋门。

normal.en: A triumphal arch is built to honour a return.
normal.cn: 凯旋门是为纪念归来的胜利者而建。

normal.en: Triumphal is the adjective of the ceremony, triumphant of the winner.
normal.cn: triumphal 形容仪式，triumphant 形容得胜者。

normal.en: Triumph over is the usual phrase for beating a difficulty.
normal.cn: triumph over 是战胜困难的常用搭配。

normal.en: The Romans borrowed the word from a Greek song in procession.
normal.cn: 罗马人是从希腊列队所唱的颂歌里借来这个词的。

normal.en: A bridge or a painting can be called a triumph too.
normal.cn: 一座桥或一幅画也可以称得上杰作。

abstract.en: Picture a general in a chariot with the crowd shouting.
abstract.cn: 想象将军站在战车上，人群呼喊。

abstract.en: See flower wreaths hanging from the carriage rails.
abstract.cn: 看花环从车栏上垂下来。

abstract.en: Hear the horns and keep that noise for the word.
abstract.cn: 听号角声，把这份热闹留给这个词。

examples.en: The victory parade marked the triumph of the long campaign.
examples.cn: 胜利游行标志着这场长期战役的凯旋。

examples.en: She triumphed over her fear of water at forty.
examples.cn: 她四十岁时战胜了对水的恐惧。

examples.en: The new library is a triumph of quiet design.
examples.cn: 新图书馆是静默设计的杰作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「揣安姆」——揣着奖杯放心安下来，姆指一竖就是胜利。

root: 拉丁语 triumphus（凯旋式），可能借自希腊语 thriambos（列队唱的酒神颂），经古法语进入英语；同族有 triumphal、triumphant

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from the Roman procession to a private feeling and to any finished masterpiece.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项从罗马的凯旋式，一路走到个人的感受与任何完成后的杰作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a victor riding through a shouting city.
core.cn: 核心意象：胜利者穿过欢呼的城。

branches.en: The victory sense, the plain fact of winning.
branches.cn: 胜利义：取胜这一事实本身。

branches.en: The feeling sense, where the celebration goes inward.
branches.cn: 情绪义：欢庆转到了心里。

branches.en: The verb sense, where a person overcomes something.
branches.cn: 动词义：人克服了某物。

branches.en: The achievement sense, where a work earns the ovation.
branches.cn: 成就义：一件作品赢得了欢呼。

branches.en: The victory sense again, where the parade begins.
branches.cn: 再回胜利义：游行的起点。

intro.en: The word came whole from Latin, and its endings were already in place.
intro.cn: 这个词是从拉丁语整体借来的，词尾早就带在身上。

latinIntro.en: Triumphus has no common Latin verb behind it in English use, so the Latin list gives only the noun.
latinIntro.cn: triumphus 在英语用法里没有常见拉丁动词相配，因此拉丁同源词只列名词。

items.example: In triumph the -ant marks the feeling, not the person.
items.exampleCN: 在 triumph 里，-ant 标记的是情绪而非人。

items.meaning: the written ph stands for the f sound
items.meaningCN: ph 写法表示 f 音
items.example: Triumph ends in ph, as in triumph and nymph.
items.exampleCN: triumph 以 ph 收尾，如同 nymph。

items.example: The arch stands at the road’s end.

items.meaningCN: 王牌；与 triumph 只是拼写相近
items.example: Trump looks like triumph but is another word.
items.exampleCN: trump 看着像 triumph，却是另一个词。

definition_zh: 部队；一群；成群结队地走；军队
definition_en: a group of soldiers, or a group of people or animals moving together
core_image: 一队人排着走，脚步一同落下，扬起一小片尘土
scene: 清晨的操场上，一排士兵沿着跑道走成一列，背囊轻轻晃动。The troop moved slowly along the ridge at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 troop 是「部队、一队士兵」（第 1 个义项：成队行动的军人）；句意为部队在黎明时沿山脊缓缓行进。整齐同行的一队人正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 名词加 -er 构成，义为「骑兵；州警」
现在分词名词化，义为「列队行进」
合成词，义为「运兵车；运兵舰」

senses.title: A group of soldiers
senses.definition: a group of soldiers, especially a unit of cavalry or a body of troops in action
senses.definitionCN: 一队士兵，尤指骑兵单位或行动中的队伍
senses.example: The troop was ordered back to the base.
senses.exampleCN: 这支部队被命令返回基地。
senses.why: A troop is first a small body of riders, and the word keeps that picture of a band moving as one.
senses.whyCN: troop 最初指一小队骑手，这个词始终保留「一伙人走成一体」的画面。

senses.title: Soldiers in general
senses.definition: soldiers considered as a body, especially those sent to a place
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体的士兵，尤指派往某地的兵力
senses.example: Troops were sent to the border.
senses.exampleCN: 部队被派往边境。
senses.why: The plural widens the single unit into the whole body of soldiers on a front.
senses.whyCN: 复数把单个单位扩展成前线上的全部兵力。

senses.title: A group of people or animals
senses.definition: a group of people or animals moving together
senses.definitionCN: 一起行动的一群人或一群动物
senses.example: A troop of schoolchildren crossed the square.
senses.exampleCN: 一群小学生穿过广场。
senses.why: A band of soldiers is a band, and any other band moving together borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 一队士兵本就是一伙人，其他成伙走动的也用这个名字。

senses.title: To move in a group
senses.definition: to walk somewhere in a group, often without much order
senses.definitionCN: 成群地往某处走，常显得杂乱
senses.example: The children trooped into the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们成群地涌进礼堂。
senses.why: The verb is the noun set in motion: a troop walking becomes to troop.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是让名词走起来：一队人走路就成了 troop。

senses.title: A cavalry unit in the army
senses.definition: a small mounted or armoured unit forming part of a squadron or battalion
senses.definitionCN: 骑兵或装甲部队里的小单位，属中队或营建制
senses.example: The troop formed up at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 这个骑兵连在门口集合。
senses.why: Military organisation keeps the oldest sense, a small body of riders.
senses.whyCN: 军队编制保留了最古老的义项：一小队骑手。

intro.en: The word comes from French troupe, a band or company, and is probably of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: 这个词来自法语 troupe（一伙、一队），大概源出日耳曼语。

items.en: Troupe means a band, a company, or a crowd, and is used of soldiers and of players.
items.cn: 法语 troupe 意为一伙、一队、一群人，既用于士兵也用于演员。

items.en: The French word probably goes back to a Germanic root meaning a crowd or a herd.
items.cn: 这个法语词可能追溯到日耳曼语里表示人群或畜群词根。

items.en: English borrows it in the sixteenth century for a body of soldiers.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，指一队士兵。

items.en: The plural troops becomes the ordinary word for soldiers sent to a place.
items.cn: 其复数 troops 成了「派往某地的兵力」的通常说法。

items.en: The word also names a small cavalry unit and any group of animals or children.
items.cn: 这个词也指小型骑兵单位，以及任何一群动物或孩子。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the troupe spelling family, while the near-meaning group gathers other words for armed bodies and groups.
note.cn: 形近组同属 troupe 拼写家族，近义组汇集其他军队与群体的说法。

entries.definition: a company of actors or performers
a soldier in a cavalry or armoured unit
a curved shape closing on itself
a prize won in a contest
the whole military force of a country
a small organised part of an army
a large number of people together
a group of animals feeding or moving together

normalIntro.en: Troop and troupe are the same word split two ways: soldiers and players.
normalIntro.cn: troop 与 troupe 是同一个词的两条路：一边是兵，一边是演员。

normal.en: The plural troops is the everyday word for soldiers abroad.
normal.cn: 复数 troops 是「驻外部队」的日常说法。

normal.en: A trooper is the soldier in the troop.
normal.cn: trooper 就是队伍里的兵。

normal.en: Troupe keeps the French spelling for a company of actors.
normal.cn: troupe 保留法语拼法，指剧团。

normal.en: The verb usually goes with into or out of: they trooped out.
normal.cn: 动词常与 into 或 out of 连用：他们成群走出。

normal.en: A troop of monkeys works the same way as a troop of soldiers.
normal.cn: 一群猴子与一队士兵的用法相同。

abstract.en: Picture a line of soldiers walking a ridge at first light.
abstract.cn: 想象天刚亮时一列士兵走在山脊上。

abstract.en: Hear the boots land almost together.
abstract.cn: 听靴子几乎同时落地。

abstract.en: Then see a class of children do exactly the same on a stair.
abstract.cn: 再看一班孩子在同一段楼梯上做同样的动作。

examples.en: Fresh troops arrived at the front before winter.
examples.cn: 入冬前新部队抵达前线。

examples.en: A troop of monkeys crossed the road in single file.
examples.cn: 一群猴子排成一列过了马路。

examples.en: After the bell, the class trooped out into the yard.
examples.cn: 铃响后，全班成群涌到院子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「出普」——一出营门就排成普普通通的一队人。

root: 法语 troupe（一伙、一队），可能源自日耳曼语「人群」词根，十六世纪进入英语；同族有 troupe、trooper

sensesIntro.en: Every sense names a body of beings moving together, from cavalry to schoolchildren.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都指一起行动的一群，从骑兵到小学生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: boots landing almost together along a ridge.
core.cn: 核心意象：靴子几乎同时落在山脊上。

branches.en: The soldier senses, where a small unit is meant.
branches.cn: 士兵义：指的是具体的小单位。

branches.en: The force sense, where the plural means all the soldiers there.
branches.cn: 兵力义：复数指当地全部士兵。

branches.en: The group sense, where children or animals form the band.
branches.cn: 群体义：孩子或动物组成这一伙。

branches.en: The verb sense, where the band starts walking.
branches.cn: 动词义：这一伙动起来了。

branches.en: The unit sense again, where the formation is what counts.
branches.cn: 再回单位义：关键在队形。

intro.en: The word is French in shape, and the family around it is small and concrete.
intro.cn: 这个词带法语形状，周围的词族小而具体。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin relative in English, so the Latin list here stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 它在英语里没有拉丁亲族，所以这里的拉丁同源词留空。

items.meaning: a vehicle or ship for soldiers
items.example: The troop carrier left at dawn.

items.meaning: to walk out in a group
items.example: They trooped out of the hall.

items.meaning: the ceremony of marching the colours
items.example: Trooping the colour is held in June.
items.exampleCN: 军旗列队仪式在六月举行。

definition_zh: 麻烦；困难；烦扰；使烦恼；疾病
definition_en: a problem or difficulty, or the act of making someone worried or upset
core_image: 水面被搅得浑起来，鱼看不见，连倒影都碎了
scene: 深夜，修车师傅蹲在路边，车前盖敞开着，车主来回踱步打电话。The old car has given us a lot of trouble this year.
sceneCN: 这里 trouble 是「麻烦」（第 1 个义项：让人头疼的问题）；句意为这辆旧车今年给我们添了不少麻烦。搅浑的水面与来回踱步的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 名词加 -some 构成形容词，义为「麻烦的；讨厌的」
过去分词形容词化，义为「困扰的；动荡的」
合成词，义为「惹麻烦的人」

senses.title: A problem or difficulty
senses.definition: a problem, difficulty, or unpleasant situation that must be dealt with
senses.definitionCN: 需要处理的难题、困难或令人不快的处境
senses.example: We had trouble finding the address.
senses.exampleCN: 我们找这个地址费了点劲。
senses.why: The verb behind the word means to stir up or disturb, and a stirred situation becomes a problem.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的动词意为搅动、扰乱，被搅乱的情形就成了麻烦。

senses.title: Worry or distress
senses.definition: a feeling of worry, anxiety, or unhappiness
senses.definitionCN: 担忧、焦虑或不快的情绪
senses.example: Her troubles seemed to lift after the call.
senses.exampleCN: 那通电话之后她的烦恼似乎散了。
senses.why: The stir that clouds the water also clouds the mind, so the word names inner unrest.
senses.whyCN: 搅浑水面的动荡同样会搅浑心里，所以这个词也指内心的不安。

senses.title: To cause someone worry
senses.definition: to make someone worried, annoyed, or uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 使某人担忧、不快或不安
senses.example: The noise troubled her all night.
senses.exampleCN: 那噪声扰了她一整夜。
senses.why: To trouble is to stir someone up, exactly as a stick stirs a pond.
senses.whyCN: trouble 就是把人搅动起来，正如一根棍子搅动池塘。

senses.title: Illness or a fault in a machine
senses.definition: an illness, or a fault in a machine or a part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 疾病，或机器、身体某部位出的毛病
senses.example: He has heart trouble and walks slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 他有心脏病，走路很慢。
senses.why: A body or an engine that is not running smoothly is in a disturbed state, so it has a trouble.
senses.whyCN: 身体或发动机运转不顺就是处于被扰动的状态，于是有了毛病。

senses.title: Extra effort taken to help
senses.definition: extra effort that one takes in order to do something for others
senses.definitionCN: 为他人做事而额外花的力气
senses.example: She took the trouble to write by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 她不嫌麻烦地手写了信。
senses.why: Stirring up effort on someone’s behalf is also a trouble, and the phrase keeps that effort visible.
senses.whyCN: 为别人搅起一番力气也是一种 trouble，这个短语把那份力气显出来。

intro.en: The word goes back through Old French to late Latin turbulare, to stir up, from turbare, to disturb.
intro.cn: 这个词经古法语回溯到晚期拉丁语 turbulare（搅动），源于 turbare（扰乱）。

items.en: Turba means a crowd, a tumult, or a disturbance, and turbare means to throw into confusion.
items.cn: 拉丁语 turba 意为人群、骚动、扰乱，动词 turbare 意为使混乱。

items.en: Turbulare, to stir up, is formed on turba and gives the later Romance words.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 turbulare（搅动）由 turba 构成，生出后来的罗曼语词。

items.en: Old French troubler means to disturb and also to make a liquid cloudy.
items.cn: 古法语 troubler 意为扰乱，也指把液体搅浑。

items.en: English borrows the noun and verb in the thirteenth century with both the literal and the mental sense.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入名词与动词，字面义与心理义一并带入。

items.en: Engineering and medicine give it the concrete senses of a fault and an illness.
items.cn: 工程与医学给了它「故障」与「疾病」两个具体义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin turb- family, while the near-meaning group names other problems and worries.
note.cn: 形近组汇集同出拉丁语 turb- 词族的词，近义组列出其他问题与烦恼的说法。

entries.definition: causing difficulty or annoyance
worried or full of conflict
full of sudden violent movement
to interrupt or upset someone
a matter that is hard to solve
the state of being hard to do
a state of anxious thought
a person or thing that annoys

normalIntro.en: The b turns to bl before the ending, and the word keeps the picture of stirred water.
normalIntro.cn: 词尾前 b 变成 bl，这个词始终带着搅水的画面。

normal.en: Troublesome adds -some and means full of trouble.
normal.cn: troublesome 加 -some，意为满是麻烦。

normal.en: Have trouble doing takes the -ing form after it.
normal.cn: have trouble doing 后面接动名词。

normal.en: Troubled is the adjective for a worried face or a troubled time.
normal.cn: troubled 形容人的忧色或动荡的时期。

normal.en: Turbulent and disturb share the same Latin root.
normal.cn: turbulent 与 disturb 共用同一个拉丁词根。

normal.en: The verb takes a direct object: the news troubled him.
normal.cn: 这个动词带宾语：那消息让他不安。

abstract.en: Picture a stick stirring a clear pond into brown.
abstract.cn: 想象一根棍子把清澈的池塘搅成褐色。

abstract.en: Watch the reflection break into pieces.
abstract.cn: 看倒影碎成一片片。

abstract.en: Wait until it settles, and the water is clear again.
abstract.cn: 等它静下来，水又清了。

examples.en: She had great trouble getting the machine to start.
examples.cn: 她费了好大劲才把机器发动起来。

examples.en: His back trouble keeps him from lifting boxes.
examples.cn: 他的背疾让他不能搬箱子。

examples.en: The question troubled her for days.
examples.cn: 那个问题困扰了她好几天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿不了」——鞋挤得穿不了，真是麻烦。

root: 拉丁语 turba（骚动）+ turbare（扰乱）→ 晚期拉丁语 turbulare → 古法语 troubler；同族有 turbulent、disturb

sensesIntro.en: The senses all come from a stirred thing: water, a mind, a body, or a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都来自被搅动的东西：水、心、身体，或机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stick stirring a clear pond until it is brown.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根棍子把清水搅成褐色。

branches.en: The plain problem sense, where affairs are stirred.
branches.cn: 麻烦义：被搅的是事情。

branches.en: The mind pair: worry felt and worry caused.
branches.cn: 心理一对：心里的烦与被搅起的烦。

branches.en: The concrete sense, where a body or a machine is disturbed.
branches.cn: 具体义：被扰动的是身体或机器。

branches.en: The effort sense, where stirring up work is meant.
branches.cn: 用力义：搅起的是一番力气。

branches.en: The problem sense again, where the water will not settle.
branches.cn: 再回麻烦义：水一时沉不下去。

intro.en: The word is Latin in origin, and the family around it is short but active.
intro.cn: 这个词源出拉丁，周围的词族短小却活跃。

latinIntro.en: Turba and turbare lie behind trouble, turbulent, and disturb.
latinIntro.cn: turba 与 turbare 支撑着 trouble、turbulent 与 disturb。

items.exampleCN: 他们生活在动荡的年代。

items.example: The turbine spins in the stream.
He was known as a troublemaker.
items.exampleCN: 他是出了名的麻烦制造者。
没有麻烦的一周很少见。

definition_zh: 麻烦的；令人烦恼的；棘手的；讨厌的
definition_en: causing trouble, difficulty, or annoyance
core_image: 一扇门关不严，风一吹就咯咯响，怎么修都不服帖
scene: 课堂上，后排两个学生一直传纸条，老师几次停下来看他们。The troublesome noise from the pipes kept the whole floor awake.
sceneCN: 这里 troublesome 是「令人烦恼的」（第 1 个义项：带来麻烦、令人不快）；句意为管道传来的恼人噪声让整层楼都睡不着。关不严的门反复作响正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：麻烦的；令人烦恼的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「麻烦地；令人烦恼地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「麻烦；棘手」
去掉 -some 的基础名词，义为「麻烦」

senses.title: Causing annoyance
senses.definition: causing annoyance or difficulty, especially again and again
senses.definitionCN: 反复带来烦恼或困难
senses.example: The troublesome tap drips all night.
senses.exampleCN: 那个讨厌的水龙头滴了一整夜。
senses.why: The suffix -some means causing, so the word says plainly that trouble is being caused.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -some 意为「引起」，所以这个词直说：麻烦正在被引起。

senses.title: Hard to deal with
senses.definition: difficult to handle, solve, or control
senses.definitionCN: 难以处理、解决或控制的
senses.example: The border issue is a troublesome one.
senses.exampleCN: 边境问题是个棘手的问题。
senses.why: A problem earns the suffix when every solution costs more than it seems worth.
senses.whyCN: 一道难题一旦每个解法都代价高过所值，就配上了这个词尾。

senses.title: Behaving badly
senses.definition: of a person, often behaving badly and causing work for others
senses.definitionCN: 指人常常胡闹、给别人添事
senses.example: He was a troublesome pupil in his first year.
senses.exampleCN: 他第一年是个难管的学生。
senses.why: A person who keeps causing work is someone who keeps causing trouble, so -some fits again.
senses.whyCN: 常给人添活的人就是常惹麻烦的人，所以 -some 依然合适。

intro.en: The word is English through and through: the noun trouble plus the suffix -some, causing.
intro.cn: 这个词彻头彻尾是英语自造：名词 trouble 加上意为「引起」的后缀 -some。

items.en: Troubler supplies the base noun and verb, meaning to disturb.
items.cn: 古法语 troubler 提供了基础名词与动词，意为扰乱。

items.en: The noun trouble is in use by the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 trouble 在十三世纪已在使用。

items.en: The suffix -some forms adjectives from nouns, as in handsome and tiresome.
items.cn: 后缀 -some 由名词构成形容词，如 handsome 与 tiresome。

items.en: Troublesome is recorded from the sixteenth century with the sense of causing trouble.
items.cn: troublesome 从十六世纪起有记录，意为引起麻烦。

items.en: It now covers things, times, and people that are hard to manage.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖难对付的事物、时期与人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other -some adjectives, while the near-meaning group names other words for annoying things.
note.cn: 形近组汇集其他 -some 形容词，近义组列出其他表示恼人的词。

entries.definition: a problem or difficulty
making you feel tired and bored
causing slight annoyance
good looking; the suffix is shared, the meaning differs
entries.definitionCN: 英俊的；只是词尾相同，意思不同

entries.definition: making you feel slightly angry
causing difficulty to solve
hard to deal with
causing no damage or trouble

normalIntro.en: Trouble plus -some, and -some always means causing.
normalIntro.cn: trouble 加 -some，而 -some 总是表示「引起」。

normal.en: Tiresome, bothersome, and troublesome share one suffix.
normal.cn: tiresome、bothersome、troublesome 共用同一个词尾。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable: TROUB-lesome.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节：TROUB-lesome。

normal.en: The adverb adds -ly and the noun adds -ness.
normal.cn: 副词加 -ly，名词加 -ness。

normal.en: The word can describe things, times, and people alike.
normal.cn: 这个词既可形容事物、时期，也可形容人。

normal.en: Its base noun takes no article when used in the abstract.
normal.cn: 作抽象用法时，它的基础名词不带冠词。

abstract.en: Picture a door that will not shut properly.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇怎么也关不严的门。

abstract.en: Hear it rattle whenever the wind comes past.
abstract.cn: 听风一过就咯咯作响。

abstract.en: Feel how that sound keeps nagging at the ear.
abstract.cn: 体会那声音怎样一直磨着耳朵。

examples.en: The cough proved more troublesome than the fever.
examples.cn: 咳嗽比发烧更让人难受。

examples.en: They found the tax rules particularly troublesome.
examples.cn: 他们发现税务规定特别棘手。

examples.en: A troublesome cough kept him off work for a week.
examples.cn: 一场讨厌的咳嗽让他一周没能上班。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿了不松」——鞋穿了不松，却磨脚磨得烦人。

root: trouble（拉丁语 turba「骚动」经古法语）+ 后缀 -some（引起……的），英语自造词

sensesIntro.en: The suffix links all three senses: whatever or whoever keeps causing trouble.
sensesIntro.cn: 词尾把三个义项串起来：凡是不停引起麻烦的东西或人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door that will not shut and rattles in the wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇关不严的门，风里咯咯作响。

branches.en: The annoyance sense, where the trouble is a sound or a fault.
branches.cn: 烦人义：麻烦是声音或毛病。

branches.en: The difficult sense, where the trouble is a problem.
branches.cn: 棘手义：麻烦是一道难题。

branches.en: The personal sense, where the trouble is a person.

branches.en: The mixture, where a fault becomes a problem for everyone.

definition_zh: 裤子；长裤
definition_en: a piece of clothing worn over the waist and legs, with a part for each leg
core_image: 两条布筒从上边连到腰上，人一迈步就分开又合拢
scene: 衣柜前，他把一条深灰色的裤子抖开，对着镜子比了比裤腿的长短。These trousers are too long; I shall have them shortened.
sceneCN: 这里 trousers 是「长裤」（第 1 个义项：遮住腰与两腿、各有一条腿管的裤子）；句意为这条裤子太长了，我要拿去改短。两条布筒从腰部垂下正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 去掉词尾 -s 作定语用，义为「裤子的」
加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「穿着裤子的」
加 -less 构成形容词，义为「没穿裤子的」

senses.title: A garment for the legs
senses.definition: a garment that covers the body from the waist to the ankles, with two legs
senses.definitionCN: 从腰盖到脚踝、分两条腿管的衣物
senses.example: He wears grey trousers to work.
senses.exampleCN: 他上班穿灰色长裤。
senses.why: The two legs of the garment make it a plural word in English and in French.
senses.whyCN: 这件衣物有两条腿，所以英语和法语里都用作复数形式。

senses.title: Trousers as part of a uniform
senses.definition: the leg-worn part of a formal uniform, often with a stripe
senses.definitionCN: 正装制服里成套的裤装，常带侧条纹
senses.example: The officer’s trousers carry a red stripe.
senses.exampleCN: 军官的制服裤上有道红条。
senses.why: A uniform makes the legs of one garment a mark of rank, so the plural keeps its force.
senses.whyCN: 制服让这一件裤装成了身份的标记，复数形式因此依旧。

senses.title: The adjective use before another noun
senses.definition: used as an attributive word meaning of or for trousers
senses.definitionCN: 作定语，表示「裤子的」或「用于裤子的」
senses.example: The trouser leg is torn at the knee.
senses.exampleCN: 裤腿膝盖处破了。
senses.why: English drops the final s when the word becomes a modifier, as in trouser leg.
senses.whyCN: 这个词作修饰语时英语会去掉末尾的 s，如 trouser leg。

intro.en: The word comes from French pantalon and its like, but trousers itself is from Irish or Gaelic trews, the older form of the garment.
intro.cn: 这个词的现代形来自「trews」——盖尔语系里指裤子的老词，后受法语形制影响而定形。

items.en: The older form trews, from Irish and Scottish Gaelic triubhas, names close-fitting legwear.
items.cn: 更早的形式 trews 出自爱尔兰语与苏格兰盖尔语 triubhas，指紧身裤装。

items.en: English borrows trews in the sixteenth century for tight hose worn under a tunic.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 trews，指穿在外衣下的一种紧身裤。

items.en: The ending of the word is reshaped after French forms ending in -ous.
items.cn: 这个词的结尾受法语 -ous 一类形式影响而被改写。

items.en: Trousers replaces breeches in the nineteenth century as the ordinary word for long legwear.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，trousers 取代 breeches 成为长裤的通常说法。

items.en: It stays plural though it names one garment, as do scissors and glasses.
items.cn: 它指一件衣物却仍用复数，如同 scissors 与 glasses。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers garments and near spellings, while the near-meaning group names related items of clothing.
note.cn: 形近组汇集衣物类词与相近拼写，近义组列出相关服饰说法。

normalIntro.en: Two legs make a plural word, and English keeps the s.
normalIntro.cn: 两条腿让它成了复数词，英语保留了末尾的 s。

normal.en: A pair of trousers takes a plural verb: these trousers are long.
normal.cn: 一条裤子用复数动词：these trousers are long。

normal.en: Before another noun the s usually drops: trouser leg.
normal.cn: 作定语时常去掉 s：trouser leg。

normal.en: Jeans and shorts are the same kind of plural garment word.
normal.cn: jeans 与 shorts 是同类复数衣物词。

normal.en: The older form trews survives in Scottish English.
normal.cn: 更早的形式 trews 仍见于苏格兰英语。

normal.en: Count them with a pair of, never with a single number.
normal.cn: 用 a pair of 计数，不用单个数字。

abstract.en: Picture two cloth tubes joined at the waist, splitting at the knee.
abstract.cn: 想象两条布筒在腰上相连，到膝上分开。

abstract.en: Hear the cloth swish as one leg passes the other.
abstract.cn: 听一腿越过另一腿时布料的沙沙声。

abstract.en: Then think of a wardrobe where one item has two doors.
abstract.cn: 再想衣柜里一件衣物有两个门洞。

intro.en: The word is Celtic in origin, and its English family is built with plain endings.
